headline: Learn Odin Programming Language with a new book by Karl Zylinski
summary: Explore basic and advanced Odin concepts, including manual memory management and data-oriented design, in this comprehensive guide.
details: A new book titled "Understanding the Odin Programming Language" is now available, aimed at individuals with prior programming experience looking to delve into low-level programming.

Authored by Karl Zylinski, an independent game developer and educator, the book covers fundamental and advanced Odin concepts such as procedures, manual memory management, parametric polymorphism, and data-oriented design.
The book emphasizes not just how to write Odin code, but also the underlying reasons for the language's design, helping readers become more proficient programmers by understanding their tools.
It is presented in a portable HTML format, designed for an optimal reading experience on computers, but also accessible on phones and tablets, with all fonts and images included.

Karl Zylinski is known for creating "CAT & ONION," the first commercial video game developed in Odin, and shares educational content on his YouTube channel. He has a background in game engine programming for companies like Autodesk and has worked as a game programmer at Hazelight and Our Machinery.
The latest version of the book features significant revisions and expansions to the strings chapter (chapter 11), along with numerous other changes to enhance clarity throughout the text.

Readers can purchase the book in HTML+eBook format from store.zylinski.se or Itch, with recommendations to buy from these platforms to receive both versions. Updates can be obtained by re-downloading the purchased copy.

headline_marked: AI agents [[revive 25-year-old math applets]] with graphical upgrades
headline: AI agents revive 25-year-old math applets with graphical upgrades
summary: Modern AI coding assistants successfully ported legacy Java applets to Javascript, restoring functionality and even adding new visual features after two decades.
details: A mathematician has successfully used modern AI coding agents to revive and enhance mathematical applets he originally created in 1999. These applets, developed in Java 1.0 for complex analysis and linear algebra courses, had become non-functional due to outdated web standards.

The AI agent was tasked with porting the applets to Javascript, a modern, supported language. In just a few hours, the agent not only restored the functionality of over two dozen applets but also introduced graphical improvements, such as colorizing a previously monochrome visualization.

Among the revived applets is a particularly complex honeycomb visualization, originally coded with Allen Knutson in 1999. The AI's ability to handle such intricate code was notable, with the developer finding only one minor bug in the ported code, while the AI even identified two pre-existing bugs in the original.

Encouraged by the success, the mathematician also experimented with creating new visualizations. An ambitious project from 1999, a visualization tool for special relativity, was finally realized after a couple of hours of 'vibe coding' with an AI agent, resulting in an applet matching the original vision.

Furthermore, an AI agent was used to generate an interactive visualization for the Gilbreath conjecture paper, demonstrating the potential for AI-assisted supplements to academic work. The developer plans to incorporate such interactive visualizations in future papers, deeming the risk of using AI-generated code acceptable for non-critical components.
